name: Old Kingdom Egypt

P2a_tech_diffusion.justification: Pyramid construction, copper metallurgy, papyrus — diffusion mainly court-centered

P3a_life_expect.justification: LE at birth ~28-32 yrs from skeletal/mortuary data

P4a_gdp_proxy.justification: Estimated ~$500-600 GK$ for Nile agrarian economy with monumental surplus

P4b_trade_auton.source: Sowada 2009, Egypt in the Eastern Mediterranean during the Old Kingdom
P4b_trade_auton.justification: Significant Levantine/Nubian trade but not dependent; state-managed

P4c_tribute_dep.source: Moreno García 2013, 'The Territorial Administration of the Kingdom' in AEA
P4c_tribute_dep.justification: Nubian gold/resources significant; not fully autonomous of peripheral extraction

P5a_regime_dur.source: Shaw (ed.) 2003, Oxford History of Ancient Egypt

P1b_legal_formal.justification: Royal writ ineffective beyond Memphis region; local customs supersede

P1c_bureaucratic.justification: Offices deeply hereditary; Pepi II's 94-yr reign ossified appointments

P1d_fiscal_std.source: Kanawati 1980, Governmental Reforms in Old Kingdom Egypt
P1d_fiscal_std.justification: Tax collection fragmented; nome-level retention rising

P2a_tech_diffusion.justification: No significant technological regression yet

P2b_knowledge_inst.justification: Provincial scribal traditions continuing

P3a_life_expect.justification: Possible slight decline from 4.2ka drought stress

P3b_elite_literacy.justification: No major change in literacy rates

P4a_gdp_proxy.justification: Agricultural output declining with Nile low-floods

P4b_trade_auton.justification: Trade continuing but state share declining

P4c_tribute_dep.justification: Nubian extraction disrupted

P5a_regime_dur.justification: Dynasty still nominally intact

P5b_succession.justification: Pepi II's extreme reign created contested succession; ephemeral Dynasty VII/VIII
